title: Approximation by a Probability Density
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varphi$ be a nonnegative probability density of uniform expectation one on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, let $C$ be a set of real-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$. The density $\varphi$ fools $C$ to error $\varepsilon$ if, for every $f\in C$, the absolute difference between the expectation of $f$ under $\varphi$ and its uniform expectation is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $\varphi$ is a pointwise nonnegative probability density with uniform expectation one
$C$ is a set of real-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
For every $f\in C$, the absolute expectation difference is at most $\varepsilon$
